# HDivergingBarChart

> Slender percentage bars above and below zero, with a fixed ±100% scale and exact-value inspection.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.9.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HDivergingBarChart` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-diverging-bar-chart>`.
- Constructor: `HearthDivergingBarChartElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HDivergingBarChart.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Values are percentage points, not fractions: 35 means +35%, and -55 means -55%. Positive bars rise above the zero center line; negative bars extend below it. The fixed range is -100% to +100%, so identical values keep their scale as new points arrive. Out-of-range bars cap at the scale boundary while tooltips and the data table retain exact values. Nonfinite values render as zero, and zero values have no filled bar.
- Visual bars default to 6px wide and a 96px plot; barWidth is bounded to 2–12px and height to 64–600px. Pointer targets stay 24px wide (44px on coarse pointers), without overlapping; narrow charts scroll inside their own viewport. Per-point labels live in tooltips and the data table to keep the waveform-like plot uncluttered.
- Hover or focus to inspect; arrow/Home/End keys navigate, Escape dismisses the tooltip, and activation emits select(id). selected is application-owned. positiveTone defaults to accent and negativeTone to info; direction and signed text communicate meaning beyond color. App-owned updates transition smoothly, with reduced-motion support. Shows the latest maxPoints (default 60, maximum 240).

## Public API

items: ChartPoint[] · label, description, selected: string · height: number = 96 · barWidth: number = 6 · maxPoints: number · positiveTone, negativeTone: Tone

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: ChartPoint[];
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    selected?: string;
    height?: number;
    barWidth?: number;
    maxPoints?: number;
    positiveTone?: Tone;
    negativeTone?: Tone;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{
    items: () => [],
    height: 96,
    barWidth: 6,
    positiveTone: "accent",
    negativeTone: "info",
  }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, title, axis, viewport, column, segment, tooltip, legend, data, empty

Use `hearth-diverging-bar-chart::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface ChartPoint {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    value: number;
}

export type Tone = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "info";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HDivergingBarChart } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HDivergingBarChart label="Throughput change" :items="[{id:'a',label:'09:00',value:35},{id:'b',label:'10:00',value:-55},{id:'c',label:'11:00',value:20}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-diverging-bar-chart');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Throughput change",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "a",
      "label": "09:00",
      "value": 35
    },
    {
      "id": "b",
      "label": "09:15",
      "value": -55
    },
    {
      "id": "c",
      "label": "09:30",
      "value": 20
    },
    {
      "id": "d",
      "label": "09:45",
      "value": 80
    },
    {
      "id": "e",
      "label": "10:00",
      "value": -25
    },
    {
      "id": "f",
      "label": "10:15",
      "value": 55
    },
    {
      "id": "g",
      "label": "10:30",
      "value": -70
    },
    {
      "id": "h",
      "label": "10:45",
      "value": 40
    },
    {
      "id": "i",
      "label": "11:00",
      "value": 65
    },
    {
      "id": "j",
      "label": "11:15",
      "value": -15
    },
    {
      "id": "k",
      "label": "11:30",
      "value": -40
    },
    {
      "id": "l",
      "label": "11:45",
      "value": 25
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
